# Deservingness criteria in the allocation of educational benefits in higher education: A distributional survey experiment approach.

Juan Carlos Castillo & Tomás Urzúa
Deparment of Sociology, Universidad de Chile

The social welfare literature has long debated the principles that should guide the allocation of public goods and benefits. In this context, the deservingness criteria (Knotz, 2022; Meulemann et al, 2020;Van Oorschot, 2000) have emerged as a key framework in understanding how individuals perceive the fairness of distributing benefits in different welfare domains. These criteria often include factors such as need, effort, attitude, and identity, which individuals take into account when evaluating the deservingness of others. In the present study, we aim to explore how deservingness criteria affect the decisions in benefits' allocation for access to higher education (scholarships). For this, we use a distributional survey experiment (DSE) (Gilgen, 2022), a methodology that combines the characteristics of conjoints, factorial surveys, and allocation experiments, allowing researchers to systematically manipulate the characteristics of hypothetical beneficiaries and observe how these manipulations influence respondents' allocation decisions. Our main argument is that the deservingness criterion of effort --linked to preferences for meritocracy-- would outweigh egalitarian criteria in the allocation of scholarships amounts. Using data from a novel survey experiment conducted in Chile in 2026 (N=4,500), we tested the effects of different deservingness criteria on the allocation of educational benefits, as well as how such criteria interact with individual characteristics as socio-economic status, gender, political orientation, and preferences for meritocratic distribution. The findings from this experimental approach contribute to the broader literature on social welfare and public opinion, providing insights into how individuals prioritize different factors when determining who deserves access to higher education.
